title: Conduct, dress and punctuality
summary: How a PeakAge companion shows up: on time, presentable, respectful and focused on the elder.

lessons.title: Right person, right time
lessons.body:
PeakAge's promise to families is **right person, right time**. A no-show or a late arrival breaks that promise instantly. The child far away has planned around you, and the elder is waiting dressed and ready.

- **Reach 10 minutes early.** Wait outside if needed.
- **Running late?** Call the coordinator and the family *before* the visit time, not after.
- **Can't make it?** Tell the coordinator as early as possible so a backup can go.

> A no-show without informing is a serious strike. Two strikes and you are off the platform.

lessons.title: Dress, ID and phone
lessons.body:
- **Dress:** clean, simple and modest. Wear the PeakAge T-shirt if you have one.
- **ID:** always carry your PeakAge ID card and show it when you arrive.
- **Phone:** only for the visit (updates to the child, notes, booking). No personal calls, social media or games during the visit.
- **Language:** respectful always. “Aap”, never “tum”. Uncle-ji, Aunty-ji, or how the family prefers.
- **Food and gifts:** accepting a cup of tea is polite. Don't ask for anything. Money or costly gifts are covered in the Money rules module.

lessons.title: Respect, dignity and privacy
lessons.body:
- **Sanskaar matters.** Greet with namaste. Let the elder lead. Never talk down to them, even if they are slow or confused.
- **Cultural sensitivity:** respect their religion, food habits and customs. Don't comment on them.
- **Physical help with dignity:** offer before you help (“Uncle, haath pakad loon?”). Never make them feel weak.
- **Privacy:** never post an elder's photo or story on social media. Photos are only for the report to the child. Family matters you hear stay private.
- **Never take sides** in family matters (“haan aunty, uncle galat karte hain” is a mistake).

questions.text: You'll be 15 minutes late because of traffic. When should you inform the coordinator and family?
options: Before the visit time, as soon as you know
questions.explanation: Always call before the visit time. Families plan around you.

questions.text: How early should you reach for a visit?
questions.explanation: Reach 10 minutes early so the visit starts on time.

questions.text: Aunty is sharing a long story while you wait for the doctor. A friend messages you. What do you do?
options: Reply quickly, it's just one message
Keep the phone away and keep listening
questions.explanation: No personal phone use during visits. Your attention is the service.

questions.text: Can you post a nice photo with uncle on your Instagram if he looks happy?
options: No, photos are only for the report to the child
questions.explanation: Never post elders' photos or stories on social media. Photos are only for the report.

questions.text: Aunty complains that her husband never helps at home. What is the right response?
options: Listen and empathise, without taking sides
questions.explanation: Listen with empathy, but never take sides or comment on family members.

questions.text: What happens after two no-shows without informing?
options: The companion is removed from the platform
questions.explanation: No-shows break the family's trust. Two strikes and the companion is off the platform.

questions.text: Uncle walks slowly up the stairs. What's the respectful way to help?
options: Walk ahead and wait at the top
questions.explanation: Offer before helping. Physical help should never make an elder feel weak.
